problem: Given that $y=3x-1$ for $x=x(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2$ at the point where $x=-1,$ find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3x-1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3x-1) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-1) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2$ and $x=-1,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2\cdot (3)=6.\end{aligned}
$$
